title: The Color Purple: How Do You Stand Free?

commenti.body:
I wish Hollywood would stop making this movie. Every single adaption we have gotten so far, including the Broadway show, loves removing the lesbian aspects of the story hardcore. This part of the book is so important to the story and how the characters interact and think, and we merely get hints of it from this movie and the Spielberg one. I find it extremely frustrating how they keep making this powerful lgbtq+ story into a more straight friendly wide-appealing experience. This movie is definitely better with it than the Spielberg movie, but it's still not enough.

Ontop of all of that I had a really hard time accepting this story as a musical in the first place. It's not that musicals can't be deep or cover hard topics, but the gloss of this movie made it hard for me to take it seriously as we watch this woman get abused constantly. The songs were totally spastic quality wise for me, and made the tone fly all over the place like crazy. I urge you to please read the original book if you liked this movie or the Spielberg one.

You know what, they showed a kiss and that was it, I felt there was something missing in Sugar Avery's story in particular, it didnt feel full like Sofia's story. I guess I'm going to have read the book because the story itself is very strong and inspiring.
